title: Reducing COPD’s Global Impact on Lung Health | Regeneron
summary: Learn why COPD is a growing global health challenge and how making lung health a priority in healthy aging can improve outcomes and quality of life.
body_markdown:
Second, we must work to better understand COPD. In 2024, COPD research received less than two percent of the funding that cancer received, according to the National Institutes of Health.7 There is enormous potential for discovery and improvements for patients and yet it is often deprioritized.


In September 2025, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) adopted a[political declaration](https://goldcopd.org/un-general-assembly-december-16-2025/) prioritizing prevention and response to chronic respiratory diseases, including COPD. With the tide starting to turn for COPD, it is crucial that we capitalize on this momentum as an elevated global public health priority to drive actionable implementation and real-world improvements in respiratory care.


"COPD is a notoriously challenging condition, where uncontrolled disease progressively reduces lung function, which can lead to hospitalizations, increasing the strain on people living with the disease and healthcare systems overall,” says Yamo Deniz, MD, Vice President, Global Medical Affairs, Head of Immunology & Inflammation at Regeneron. “Recent scientific advances in understanding the underlying biology of the disease may not only help people living with COPD breathe easier, but also reduce healthcare resource utilization.”


Prioritizing lung health can help reduce the development of serious chronic respiratory diseases like COPD and lessen the overall disease burden for older adults. At Regeneron, we are working with people living with COPD, global patient advocacy groups, including those that support the aging population on education and research, healthcare professionals, and other key stakeholders to clear the air on the condition. Together let’s lessen the global challenge of COPD by making lung function a main factor in the conversation on healthy aging.
